items.question: What does reading a stored value that matches no status or known old spelling return?
items.ticket: Existing values are normalised when read
items.chose: Returns null instead of throwing or guessing the nearest status.
items.instead: Throw an error, or fall back to a default status such as draft.

items.question: How much cleaning is applied to a stored value before matching (case, surrounding whitespace)?
items.ticket: Sandbox status is stored as free text (draft, Draft, in-review...)
items.chose: Trims the ends and lowercases, so "  PUBLISHED  " reads as published.
items.instead: Match case-sensitively or without trimming, or only lowercase.

items.question: How are "-", "_" and runs of spaces treated when reading?
items.chose: Collapses each run of whitespace, "-" and "_" into one space, so "-review-" reads as review and "CLAIMED__" as claimed. Inside a word the space remains, so "mer-ged" and "re   view" read as null.
items.instead: Strip separators entirely, or leave them alone and match exact spellings only.

items.question: Which old spellings count as known legacy values?
items.ticket: Sandbox status is stored as free text (draft, Draft, in-review...)
items.chose: Maps only the cleaned form "in review" to review. The "..." in the ticket's example list is not expanded to other spellings.
items.instead: Add more aliases, such as "in progress", "done" or "pending", or use no alias table.

items.question: Does writing accept a non-canonical but readable value, such as "Draft" or "in-review"?
items.chose: Accepts only exact enum strings. Anything else, including a cased variant, an untrimmed value or an old spelling, throws.
items.instead: Normalise the value with the read logic and write the canonical status.

items.question: What error does writing an invalid value raise, and what does it say?
items.chose: Throws a plain Error whose message quotes the value exactly as given.
items.instead: Throw a custom error type, or return null or a result object instead of throwing.

items.question: What happens to a row with an unreadable status in a batch read?
items.chose: Keeps the row with its id and status null instead of dropping it or failing the batch.
items.instead: Drop the row, or throw for the whole batch.

items.question: How does the batch read report the unreadable values?
items.chose: Returns a separate `unreadable` list of distinct raw stored values, exactly as stored (not cleaned), sorted with the default string sort.
items.instead: List the ids of the bad rows, list cleaned values, keep duplicates, or keep encounter order.

items.question: Does the batch read keep the input row order?
items.chose: Maps the rows one to one, so the output order matches the input.
items.instead: Group or sort the rows by status.

items.question: What does an empty or whitespace-only stored value read as?
items.chose: Reads as null, and in a batch the raw value (e.g. "  ") goes into the unreadable list.
items.instead: Read it as a default status such as draft.
